extraction.name: CONTEXTUAL
extraction.description: A Context-sensitive Text-rich visual reasoning dataset consisting of 506 challenging instructions for LMMs evaluation.
extraction.creator: Rohan Wadhawan, Hritik Bansal, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative, and existing VQA datasets, and then annotated with novel instruction-response pairs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: LAION-5B, Rico Dataset, Open WebText Initiative, InfographicVQA, STVQA, and ESTVQA datasets.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images underwent manual filtering for some categories and heuristic-based filtering using PaddleOCR for others to select images with the highest number of words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Authors were divided into two groups to annotate specific categories following guidelines. MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample, and author groups reviewed each other's samples to filter out low-quality ones.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: MTurk workers verified the correctness of each sample, finding 96% were annotated correctly. Incorrect samples were filtered out, and author groups cross-reviewed the remaining samples.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors note that linguistic diversity and writing style of human responses change with different social groups, which could impact the human baseline performance.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Human annotators were mainly from the US, which limits the linguistic diversity and writing style representation of different social groups.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating the context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models.

name.evidence: In this paper, we introduce CONTEXTUAL , a novel dataset featuring human-crafted instructions that require contextsensitive reasoning for text-rich images.

description.evidence: we propose CONTEXTUAL , aContext-sensitive Text-rich vis ualreasoning dataset consisting of 506challenging instructions for LMMs evaluation.

url.evidence: Our dataset, code, and leaderboard can be found on the project page https://con-textual.github.io/.

datePublished.evidence: Proceedings of the 41stIntemational Conference on Machine Leaming , Vienna, Austria. PMLR 235, 2024.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: CONTEXTUAL comprises images sourced from six different sources. Firstly, we obtain images for the Time ,Shopping,Navigation &Abstract categories from the LAION-5B... Secondly, we source images for the Application Usage category from the Rico Dataset... Thirdly, we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative... Lastly, we acquire images from the test sets of existing VQA datasets, and proceed to annotate them with novel instruction-response pairs.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Firstly, we obtain images for the Time ,Shopping,Navigation &Abstract categories from the LAION-5B... Secondly, we source images for the Application Usage category from the Rico Dataset... Thirdly, we scrape the website links made available by the Open WebText Initiative... Infographic , sourced from the InfographicVQA (Mathew et al., 2022) dataset, and Miscellaneous Natural Scenes , sourced from the STVQA (Biten et al., 2019) and ESTVQA (Wang et al., 2020) datasets.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The images that are categorized under Time ,Shopping ,Navigation , and Abstract undergo manual filtering to guarantee their suitability for annotation. However, for Application Usage ,Web Usage ,Infographic , andMiscellaneous Natural Scenes , we perform heuristic-based filtering. Specifically, we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image. Subsequently, we select the top 500 images with the highest number of words, a subset of which get annotated in our dataset.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: We divide the authors into two groups, namely Group 1 and Group 2, each responsible for annotating four specific categories. The authors strictly adhered to the provided annotation guidelines throughout the annotation... we asked MTurk workers... to verify the correctness of each sample... Filtering out the incorrect samples, we tasked each author group to review the samples created by the other group.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We also benchmark the performance of humans on our dataset using Amazon Mechanical Turk.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: we asked MTurk workers (mutually exclusive from the ones used for human performance baseline and human evaluation) to verify the correctness of each sample < image, instruction, response > and found that 96% of the samples were annotated correctly. Filtering out the incorrect samples, we tasked each author group to review the samples created by the other group.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: we show each model response, without revealing the model identity, to three human annotators independently.

rai:annotatorDemographics.evidence: In our experiments, we asked human annotators, mainly from the US, to provide responses to establish a human baseline.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Specifically, we employ a PaddleOCR (paddlepadle, 2023) to detect the text in the image.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: We are aware that the linguistic diversity and writing style of the human responses would change with different social groups. The extension of our work can focus on understanding the impact of different social groups on the human baseline performance on the CONTEXTUAL dataset.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We are aware that the linguistic diversity and writing style of the human responses would change with different social groups... To obtain more reliable human evaluation results, future work would involve annotators from more diverse regions.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: CONTEXTUAL is proposed to evaluate the context-sensitive text-rich visual reasoning capabilities of large multimodal models.
